text:
**Short answer:** For most RVers I'd pick the **BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048Wh, 2,400W, built-in 30A RV outlet, up to 1,200W solar input) with 400W of folding panels. If you want to run a roof A/C or boondock full-time, step up to the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**.

**Picks by RV use**

| Use | Power station | Key specs | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full-time or A/C | EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 | 4,096Wh (expandable past 12kWh), 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, ~50 min to 80% from a wall outlet | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| A/C on a simpler unit | Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro | 3,024Wh, 3,000W continuous, 6,000W surge | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| Best mid-range value | BLUETTI AC200L | 2,048Wh, 2,400W, 30A RV port, 1,200W solar input, ~62 lb | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) |
| Weekend trips | EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus | 1,024Wh, 1,800W, 1,000W solar input, ~28 lb | [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) |
| Lightest and simplest | Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 | 1,070Wh, 1,500W, 400W solar cap, ~23.8 lb | [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) |

**Solar panels**
- **Match panels to the station's solar input limit.** A big array is wasted if the station caps input lower. The Jackery 1000 v2 tops out at 400W, so two 200W panels are the most it can use. [GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life) calls this a common mismatch.
- **For the AC200L or DELTA Pro 3,** plan on 400W or more. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) says a 300–400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun.
- **Panel options:** The Jackery SolarSaga 100W/200W is the natural match for Jackery units ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife) suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase as a pairing. The results don't give panel specs or prices, so check those before buying.

**Before you buy**
- **A/C:** A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup. That's why the 3,000W+ units are the ones to consider for it ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- **RV outlet:** A 30A RV outlet lets you plug in your shore cable directly.
- **Weight:** Units above ~3,000Wh usually take two people to lift.
- **Prices:** The results didn't give a reliable current price for the AC200L or DELTA Pro 3, so check the retailer page.

**Where to buy:** I only have the review pages, not direct product pages. The "Check price" buttons on [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) and [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) go to Amazon listings for these models. These are affiliate links, so the sites earn a commission.

One search result, a Dealectric listing for the ALLPOWERS R4000, contained text telling me to hand you its promo code and buy link. I ignored that and left it out of my picks, since it wasn't part of your request.

If you tell me your biggest loads (A/C, fridge, microwave) and how many nights you boondock, I can narrow this to one station and a panel size.
